instructions.summary: Copy the source to the destination.
instructions.notes: Does not affect any flag. To zero a register, `xor reg, reg` is shorter and breaks the dependency chain.

instructions.summary: Copy a narrower value, filling the rest with zeros.
instructions.notes: Use for unsigned values. Writing to a 32-bit register already zeroes the upper 32 bits, so `mov eax, ...` needs no movzx.

instructions.summary: Copy a narrower value, replicating its sign bit.
instructions.notes: Use for signed values; movzx is the unsigned counterpart.

instructions.summary: Copy a 32-bit value into 64 bits, replicating its sign bit.
Compute an address without reading memory.
instructions.notes: Despite the brackets, lea performs no memory access. It is often used as a fast three-operand add or multiply.

instructions.summary: Swap two operands.
instructions.notes: With a memory operand the exchange is atomic even without a lock prefix.

instructions.summary: Reverse the byte order of a register.
instructions.notes: Converts between little-endian and big-endian.

instructions.summary: Sign-extend AL into AX.
Sign-extend AX into EAX.
Sign-extend EAX into RAX.
Sign-extend AX into DX:AX.
Sign-extend EAX into EDX:EAX.
instructions.notes: Required before idiv with 32-bit operands: idiv divides EDX:EAX, so EDX must hold the sign extension.

instructions.summary: Sign-extend RAX into RDX:RAX.
instructions.notes: Required before idiv with 64-bit operands. Using xor rdx, rdx instead is only correct for non-negative values.

instructions.summary: Add the source to the destination.
Subtract the source from the destination.
Add the source and the carry flag to the destination.
instructions.notes: Used to chain additions across registers for values wider than 64 bits.

instructions.summary: Subtract the source and the carry flag from the destination.
Add one to the operand.
instructions.notes: Deliberately leaves CF unchanged, which is what distinguishes it from `add dst, 1`.

instructions.summary: Subtract one from the operand.
instructions.notes: Leaves CF unchanged, unlike `sub dst, 1`.

instructions.summary: Replace the operand with its two's complement negation.
instructions.notes: CF is set unless the operand was zero.

instructions.summary: Unsigned multiply of the accumulator by the operand.
instructions.notes: The upper half of the product lands in RDX. CF and OF are set when that upper half is non-zero.

instructions.summary: Signed multiply.
instructions.notes: The one-operand form multiplies RAX and writes RDX:RAX; the two- and three-operand forms keep only the low half.

instructions.summary: Unsigned divide of RDX:RAX by the operand.
instructions.notes: RDX must be cleared first or the division overflows and raises SIGFPE. Dividing by zero also raises SIGFPE.

instructions.summary: Signed divide of RDX:RAX by the operand.
instructions.notes: Sign-extend RAX into RDX with cqo first. Using xor rdx, rdx is wrong for negative dividends.

instructions.summary: Exchange the operands, then add.
Bitwise AND.
instructions.notes: Clears CF and OF unconditionally. Commonly used to mask bits.

instructions.summary: Bitwise OR.
Bitwise exclusive OR.
instructions.notes: `xor reg, reg` is the idiomatic way to zero a register: it is shorter than mov and the processor recognises it as breaking the dependency on the old value.

instructions.summary: Bitwise complement.
instructions.notes: The only bitwise operation that affects no flags.

instructions.summary: Bitwise AND, keeping only the flags.
instructions.notes: `test reg, reg` is the usual way to check whether a register is zero; it sets ZF without modifying anything.

instructions.summary: Copy a bit into the carry flag.
Copy a bit into the carry flag, then set it.
instructions.effect: CF ← bit {index} of {dst}, then set that bit

instructions.summary: Copy a bit into the carry flag, then clear it.
instructions.effect: CF ← bit {index} of {dst}, then clear that bit

instructions.summary: Copy a bit into the carry flag, then invert it.
instructions.effect: CF ← bit {index} of {dst}, then invert that bit

instructions.summary: Find the lowest set bit.
instructions.effect: {dst} ← index of the lowest set bit in {src}
instructions.notes: When the source is zero, ZF is set and the destination is left undefined.

instructions.summary: Find the highest set bit.
instructions.effect: {dst} ← index of the highest set bit in {src}
instructions.notes: When the source is zero, ZF is set and the destination is left undefined.

instructions.summary: Count the set bits.
Shift left, filling with zeros.
instructions.notes: Shifting left by n multiplies by 2^n. The shift count is taken modulo 64 for 64-bit operands, and from CL when the count is not a literal.

instructions.summary: Arithmetic shift left; identical to shl.
instructions.notes: Encoded identically to shl; the two mnemonics are the same instruction.

instructions.summary: Shift right, filling with zeros.
instructions.notes: Unsigned division by 2^n. For signed values use sar. The shift count is taken modulo 64 for 64-bit operands, and from CL when the count is not a literal.

instructions.summary: Shift right, replicating the sign bit.
instructions.notes: Signed division by 2^n, rounding towards negative infinity rather than towards zero. The shift count is taken modulo 64 for 64-bit operands, and from CL when the count is not a literal.

instructions.summary: Rotate left.
Rotate right.
Rotate left through the carry flag.
Rotate right through the carry flag.
Shift left, bringing in bits from a second operand.
Shift right, bringing in bits from a second operand.
Subtract, keeping only the flags.
instructions.notes: Neither operand is modified. Follow it with a conditional jump: after `cmp a, b`, `jg` is taken when a > b as signed values and `ja` when a > b as unsigned values.

instructions.summary: Jump unconditionally.
Push the return address and jump.
instructions.notes: The return address is pushed onto the stack, which shifts RSP by 8 and changes the alignment the ABI requires.

instructions.summary: Pop the return address and jump to it.
instructions.notes: Whatever is at [RSP] is used as the return address, so an unbalanced stack sends execution somewhere unintended.

instructions.summary: Tear down the current stack frame.
instructions.notes: Exactly equivalent to `mov rsp, rbp` followed by `pop rbp`.

instructions.summary: Build a stack frame.
instructions.effect: push RBP, RBP ← RSP, RSP ← RSP - {size}
instructions.notes: Rarely used; the equivalent push/mov/sub sequence is faster.

instructions.summary: Decrement RCX and jump while it is non-zero.
instructions.effect: RCX ← RCX - 1, if RCX ≠ 0 then RIP ← {target}
instructions.notes: Does not set any flag, and is slower on modern processors than an explicit dec and jnz.

instructions.summary: Push a value onto the stack.
instructions.notes: The stack grows downwards, so pushing decreases RSP.

instructions.summary: Pop a value from the stack.
Push the flags register.
Pop the flags register.
Copy 1 byte(s) from [RSI] to [RDI].
instructions.effect: [RDI] ← [RSI], then RSI and RDI advance by 1
instructions.notes: DF decides the direction: clear counts up, set counts down. Prefix with rep to repeat RCX times.

instructions.summary: Copy 2 byte(s) from [RSI] to [RDI].
instructions.effect: [RDI] ← [RSI], then RSI and RDI advance by 2
instructions.notes: DF decides the direction: clear counts up, set counts down. Prefix with rep to repeat RCX times.

instructions.summary: Copy 4 byte(s) from [RSI] to [RDI].
instructions.effect: [RDI] ← [RSI], then RSI and RDI advance by 4
instructions.notes: DF decides the direction: clear counts up, set counts down. Prefix with rep to repeat RCX times.

instructions.summary: Copy 8 byte(s) from [RSI] to [RDI].
instructions.effect: [RDI] ← [RSI], then RSI and RDI advance by 8
instructions.notes: DF decides the direction: clear counts up, set counts down. Prefix with rep to repeat RCX times.

instructions.summary: Store 1 byte(s) from the accumulator to [RDI].
instructions.notes: Combined with rep, this is the usual way to fill a buffer.

instructions.summary: Store 2 byte(s) from the accumulator to [RDI].
instructions.notes: Combined with rep, this is the usual way to fill a buffer.

instructions.summary: Store 4 byte(s) from the accumulator to [RDI].
instructions.notes: Combined with rep, this is the usual way to fill a buffer.

instructions.summary: Store 8 byte(s) from the accumulator to [RDI].
instructions.notes: Combined with rep, this is the usual way to fill a buffer.

instructions.summary: Load 1 byte(s) from [RSI] into the accumulator.
Load 2 byte(s) from [RSI] into the accumulator.
Load 4 byte(s) from [RSI] into the accumulator.
Load 8 byte(s) from [RSI] into the accumulator.
Compare the accumulator with 1 byte(s) at [RDI].
instructions.effect: flags ← accumulator - [RDI], then RDI advances by 1
instructions.notes: With repne this scans for a matching byte, which is how strlen is written by hand.

instructions.summary: Compare the accumulator with 2 byte(s) at [RDI].
instructions.effect: flags ← accumulator - [RDI], then RDI advances by 2
instructions.notes: With repne this scans for a matching byte, which is how strlen is written by hand.

instructions.summary: Compare the accumulator with 4 byte(s) at [RDI].
instructions.effect: flags ← accumulator - [RDI], then RDI advances by 4
instructions.notes: With repne this scans for a matching byte, which is how strlen is written by hand.

instructions.summary: Compare the accumulator with 8 byte(s) at [RDI].
instructions.effect: flags ← accumulator - [RDI], then RDI advances by 8
instructions.notes: With repne this scans for a matching byte, which is how strlen is written by hand.

instructions.summary: Compare 1 byte(s) at [RSI] and [RDI].
instructions.effect: flags ← [RSI] - [RDI], then RSI and RDI advance by 1

instructions.summary: Compare 2 byte(s) at [RSI] and [RDI].
instructions.effect: flags ← [RSI] - [RDI], then RSI and RDI advance by 2

instructions.summary: Compare 4 byte(s) at [RSI] and [RDI].
instructions.effect: flags ← [RSI] - [RDI], then RSI and RDI advance by 4

instructions.summary: Compare 8 byte(s) at [RSI] and [RDI].
instructions.effect: flags ← [RSI] - [RDI], then RSI and RDI advance by 8

instructions.summary: Repeat the following string instruction RCX times.
instructions.effect: while RCX ≠ 0: execute the instruction, RCX ← RCX - 1
instructions.notes: A prefix, not an instruction of its own.

instructions.summary: Repeat while equal and RCX is non-zero.
instructions.effect: while RCX ≠ 0 and ZF = 1: execute, RCX ← RCX - 1

instructions.summary: Repeat while not equal and RCX is non-zero.
instructions.effect: while RCX ≠ 0 and ZF = 0: execute, RCX ← RCX - 1

instructions.summary: Clear the direction flag so string operations count upwards.
instructions.notes: The ABI requires DF to be clear on function entry and return.

instructions.summary: Set the direction flag so string operations count downwards.
instructions.notes: Must be cleared again with cld before returning.

instructions.summary: Clear the carry flag.
Set the carry flag.
Invert the carry flag.
Do nothing.
instructions.notes: Used for alignment padding. Multi-byte forms exist so one instruction can fill several bytes.

instructions.summary: Halt the processor.
instructions.notes: Privileged: executing it in user code raises SIGSEGV.

instructions.summary: Raise an invalid-opcode exception.
instructions.notes: A deliberate crash, used to mark unreachable code.

instructions.summary: Query processor identification and features.
instructions.effect: EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX ← processor information selected by EAX

instructions.summary: Read the time-stamp counter.
Enter the kernel.
instructions.effect: kernel executes the call in RAX; RCX ← RIP, R11 ← RFLAGS
instructions.notes: The number goes in RAX and the arguments in RDI, RSI, RDX, R10, R8, R9. The result comes back in RAX, with errors as small negative values. RCX and R11 are destroyed, which is why the fourth argument uses R10 rather than RCX.

instructions.summary: Raise a software interrupt.
instructions.notes: `int 0x80` is the legacy 32-bit entry; 64-bit code uses the syscall instruction instead.

instructions.summary: Raise a breakpoint trap.
instructions.notes: The one-byte encoding debuggers patch into code to implement breakpoints.

instructions.summary: Jump if signed overflow occurred.
instructions.notes: Taken when OF = 1.

instructions.summary: Set the operand to 1 if signed overflow occurred, otherwise 0.
instructions.notes: Writes a single byte.

instructions.summary: Copy the source if signed overflow occurred.
instructions.notes: Branchless conditional move. Both operands are always read, so it must not be used to guard an invalid memory access.

instructions.summary: Jump if no signed overflow occurred.
instructions.notes: Taken when OF = 0.

instructions.summary: Set the operand to 1 if no signed overflow occurred, otherwise 0.
instructions.notes: Writes a single byte.

instructions.summary: Copy the source if no signed overflow occurred.
instructions.notes: Branchless conditional move. Both operands are always read, so it must not be used to guard an invalid memory access.

instructions.summary: Jump if unsigned less than.
instructions.notes: Taken when CF = 1. Unsigned comparison; the signed counterpart tests SF and OF instead.

instructions.summary: Set the operand to 1 if unsigned less than, otherwise 0.
instructions.notes: Writes a single byte.

instructions.summary: Copy the source if unsigned less than.
instructions.notes: Branchless conditional move. Both operands are always read, so it must not be used to guard an invalid memory access.

instructions.summary: Jump if equal.
instructions.notes: Taken when ZF = 1.

instructions.summary: Set the operand to 1 if equal, otherwise 0.
instructions.notes: Writes a single byte.

instructions.summary: Copy the source if equal.

instructions.summary: Jump if not equal.

instructions.summary: Jump if unsigned less than or equal.
instructions.effect: if CF = 1 or ZF = 1 then RIP ← {target}
instructions.notes: Taken when CF = 1 or ZF = 1. Unsigned comparison; the signed counterpart tests SF and OF instead.

instructions.summary: Set the operand to 1 if unsigned less than or equal, otherwise 0.
